 JUDGMENT The Assistant Police Commissioner, Mr. Prakash R, Sheshadripuram Sub-Division, has filed the charge sheet against the accused for the offences punishable under Sec. 498A, 306 of IPC & Sec.
3(2)(v)of SC&ST Act.

2. The gist of the prosecution case as emanated from the charge sheet is that, the accused and the deceased Bhuvaneshwari are the husband and wife and they are having 3 Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 children from their wedlock and they were residing at House No.5, 14th Cross, Maruthi Layout,
Vinayaka Circle, Vyalikaval, Bengaluru.
Deceased belong to Bhovi schedule caste and the accused belong to varnier caste.
Although, it was a love marriage, differences arose between the couple for trivial reasons.
Gradually, the accused stopped working and addicted to alcohol.
He started harassing the deceased for money to consume alcohol.

3. On 17.03.2024 at about 7 p.m., the accused asked money from his deceased wife for drinking alcohol and when the deceased did not gave money, the accused abused her in filthy language,
assaulted her with hands on her left eye and also abused her stating that she belongs low caste and asked her to go out of the house or to die.

Getting frustrated with the words spoken by the accused and his behavior, feeling dejected in life, she decided to commit suicide and hence she poured kerosene on her body and set herself ablaze on fire and then her children throw water on her.
Thereafter, the father of the deceased admitted her to Victoria Hospital for treatment.
On Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 18.03.2024, while the deceased was under treatment, the PSI took her statement and on 24.03.2024 the deceased succumbed to the burnt injuries.
4. Based on the statement of the deceased, a crime case came to be registered against the accused.
The accused was arrested on 19.03.2024, remanded to J.C. Completing the investigation, the charge sheet came to be filed against the accused on 28.05.2024 before this court.
5. Accused being in J.C. was represented through his counsel Sri. K.B.S. and later he was represented by Sri.J.R.S advocate from DLSA.
On 15.07.2024, the charge was framed and read over to the accused, for which he pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.

6. The prosecution in support of its case has examined 15 witnesses as P.W.1 to 15 and got marked 32 documents as Ex.P1 to P32 and 4 Material Objects were marked as Mos.1 to Vyalikaval Ps vs Paneer Selvam on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92500410/

After closing the prosecution side evidence, Accused was examined U/S.313 of Cr.P.C. and he denied all the incriminating Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 circumstances that has appeared in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses.
7. Heard arguments on both sides and perused the entire records.

On the basis of the materials available on record, the following points arise for my consideration:
1. Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused being the husband of the deceased - Bhuvaneshwari, subjected her to mental and physical cruelly on the demand of money for drinking alcohol in the matrimonial home situated at H.No.5, near Vinayaka Circle, Vyalikaval,, Bengaluru within the jurisdiction of Vyalikaval police station, Bengaluru and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 498(A) of IPC?

2 Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that previously and also on 17.03.2024, the accused abetted/instigated the deceased Bhuvaneshwari to commit suicide and due to the excessive mental and physical cruelty caused by the accused, the deceased Bhuvaneshwari, at about 7.00pm while residing in her matrimonial home mentioned above set Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 herself ablaze by pouring kerosene upon herself in the presence of accused and on 24.03.2024 at about 6:00 am died in the hospital and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section.306 of IPC?

3 Whether the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that on the aforesaid date, time and place, the accused being fully aware that the deceased belongs to scheduled caste intentionally insulted/intimidated her and instigated her to die and committed an offence punishable up to ten year or more under IPC and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 3(2)(v) of SC & ST Act?
4
What Order?

my findings to the above points are as follows.

sentences.text: Points No.1 to 3 :- Since these points are interconnected with each other, they are taken up together for discussion to avoid repetition of facts and findings.
10. In order to establish their case, the prosecution has cited 34 witnesses in the charge sheet, out of which they examined 15 witnesses as PW1 to PW15.
PW1 is the Women Police Constable who recorded the statement of complainant/victim/deceased in the presence of Doctor.
PW2 and 3 are the witnesses to Ex.P6 mahazar drawn in the place of occurrence.
PW4 and 5 are the eye witnesses and daughters of the deceased and the witnesses to the incident.
PW6 and 7 are the witnesses to Ex.P10 inquest mahazar.
PW8 is the Doctor who certified the conditions of the deceased to give statement.
PW9 is the relative of the deceased and an inquest mahazar witness.
Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 PW10 is the mother of the deceased and circumstantial witness to the incident.
PW11 is the elder sister of the deceased and also the circumstantial witness to the incident.
PW12 is the neighbor of the deceased and circumstantial eye witness to the incident.
PW13 is the I.O. who conducted the entire investigation and submitted the charge sheet.
PW14 is the Head constable who recorded the video of the deceased while recording the statement.

11. It is settled proposition of law that the burden in a criminal trial is always on the prosecution to prove the indictment doubt.

This burden unless modified by legislative interference, continues on the shoulders of the prosecution from the beginning to the end of every criminal trial, whatever be the nature of evidence - direct or circumstantial and whatever be the defence taken up by the accused.

In the light of the afore said principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Spl.C.C.No.
888/2024 court, the evidence of PW.1 to 15 coupled with the documentary evidence, the prosecution needs to prove its case beyond reasonable doubts.

12. The Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, a Special enactment is designed to address the systemic discrimination, social exclusion, and violence faced by marginalized communities of Schedule Castes ("SC") and Scheduled Tribes ("ST").

As per Section 8 of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989, which deals with presumption as to offences.

sentences.text: It provides that if the accused was acquainted with the victim/family, the court shall presume that the accused was aware of the caste or tribal identity of the victim, unless proved otherwise.

However, in order to give rise to presumption, there should be an allegation that the victim belongs to SC/ST community and then accused Spl.C.C.No.
888/2024 is not a member of SC/ST community and he committed the offence with the knowledge that the victim is a member of SC/ST community.
It is only when these foundational facts are disclosed, the presumption under section 8 of act could be drawn.

Bearing these principles in mind,
the case of the prosecution needs to be assessed.
14. As per Ex.P1 statement of the deceased, PW1 The Women Police Constable Sandhya obtained permission from the Doctor on 18.03.2024 at 3.40 pm to record the statement of the victim.
After the doctor certifying fit mental state of the deceased, she recorded the statement of the victim in writing.
In the statement it is recorded that the victim married the accused about 20 years back and she gave birth to 03 children.
She lived happily with her husband and children.
But later her husband started consuming alcohol
, he was not looking after the needs of the family and he used to utilize all his earnings to consume alcohol.
Later he started to demand money from the victim, he used to abuse and assault her and proclaim her to go and die.
But for the sake of her children she Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 with stood all the harassment.
On 17.03.2024 around 2 pm in the afternoon she finished her work as made servant in a house and returned to home.
Around 7 pm, the accused came home and demanded money for drinking alcohol when she replied that she does not have money, he abused and slapped on her face.
He further asked the victim to go and stand on the road or else to die.
Getting frustrated with the words spoken by the accused and his behavior, getting dejected in life she decided to commit suicide.
Hence she poured kerosene and set herself ablaze on fire.
Even at that point of time, the accused proclaimed her to die and he did not tried to save her.
Later her children poured water and tried to rescue her.
When she woke up, she was admitted in the victoria hospital.
She gave statement stating that she committed suicide due to the harassment given by her husband.
15. In the background of these allegations, the IO started investigation, recorded the statements of witnesses and filed charge sheet against the accused for abetting the deceased to commit suicide.
CW9 and 10 children of the Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 deceased arrayed as eye witnesses to the incident.
CW.13, 14 and 17 are cited as circumstantial witnesses to the incident.
Hence the evidence of these witnesses with the evidence of other official witnesses assumes greater importance in assessing the case of the prosecution.
Hence I proceed to discuss the evidence of the witnesses one by one.

16. PW1 - Smt. Sandhya P.N., Women Police Costable, Vyalikaval police station, deposed that on 18.03.2024 she accompanied PSI Mr.Vijaykumar Biradar to Victoria hospital at 2:30 pm, they met the doctor between 3:50 pm to 4:45 pm and recorded the victim Smt. Bhuvaneshwari.
She further deposed that the victim was being questioned by the PSI and she was recording the answers given by her in writing, which is identified and marked at Ex.P1.
She also deposed that the Doctor was present at the time of recording of the statement.
PW1 identified Ex.P2 to 5 photographs of the victim.

PW1 admitted that Ex-D1 endorsement of the doctor on Ex.P1 was made inside the chambers.
PW1 also admitted that she did not recorded the statement of the injured in question and answer formate, but she reduced it in the form of complaint.

PW1 further admitted that she did not obtained the signature of the victim on the statement.

18. PW2 - Mr. Basavaraj and PW3 Mr. Dayananda, both deposed about drawing of Ex.P6 spot mahazar in the place of occurrence and snapping Ex.P8 and 9 photographs, also deposed about the recovery of few burnt clothes, kerosene sample and kerosene bottle by the IO.

PW4 - Miss. Kalaivani, elder daughter of the deceased and an eye witness to the incident,
deposed that her parents had quarrel and due to which her mother poured kerosene and set herself on fire.

Kum. Rajalakshmi, another daughter of the deceased deposed in the line of PW4.
She deposed that on 18.03.2024 she came to know that her mother poured kerosene and set herself on fire.
She further deposed that parents were good to each other but she does not know why her mother has committed suicide.
She does not know who harassed her mother and she did not witnessed any quarrels between her Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 father and mother and she was in her friends house at the time of the incident.
21. PW6 - Mr. Srinivas and PW7 - Mr. Elumalai, the witnesses to Ex.P10/inquest mahazar proceedings could not depose about the IO drawing inquest mahazar proceedings.
In spite of being cross examined by the learned Public Prosecutor, they failed to accept that the deceased committed suicide due the harassment given by her husband.

22. PW8 - Dr. Kiran R., the Chief Medical Officer, Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru deposed that on 19.03.2024 in the afternoon he received Ex.P11 letter from the PSI, seeking permission to record the statement of the victim.
He examined the condition of the patient and found that she was in a fit state of mind to give statement.
Thereafter in his presence, PSI went on questioning the victim about the incident and one Mr. H.C.Raghu wrote the statement of the victim.
After the completion of recording statement he affixed his signature of Ex.P12.

PW8 deposed that the victim deposed about accused Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 abused her by taking name of her caste and subjected her to Vyalikaval Ps vs Paneer Selvam on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92500410/
6 mental and physical harassment on the demand of money for drinking alcohol.
Due to the harassment given by the accused, victim poured kerosene and set herself ablaze.
23. In the cross examination made by the learned counsel for the accused PW8 admitted that the victim body was completely burnt and he assessed the rate of burning at 60%.

But PW8 denied that the victim burn up to 90%.
24.
PW9 - Mr.Palani, a relative of the deceased, deposed about the love marriage of the deceased with accused and about the marital incompatibility between the husband and wife.

He also deposed about identifying body of the deceased at Victoria hospital on 24.03.2024, but he turned hostile in respect of the accused harassing the deceased for money and subjecting her to mental and physical harassment.

25. PW10 - Smt.Kanniyamma, the mother of the deceased deposed that the deceased loved, eloped and married the accused, thereafter she does not know much about Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 their marital lives, because she was not going her house.
She came to know through some one that the deceased attempted to commit suicide and hence she went to the hospital.
26. PW.10 was treated as hostile and subjected to cross examination in respect of the allegations made against the accused.
PW10 denied all the suggestions tendered to the contra and she denied that the accused harassed the deceased for money and abetted her to commit suicide.
She denied that she gave Ex.P15/statement before the police.
Smt. Bhagyalakshmi, the elder sister of the deceased, deposed in the line of her mother i.e., PW10 also turned hostile to the prosecution case.
Despite being cross examined by the leaned Public Prosecutor, she did not accepted any of the suggestions made on behalf of the prosecution.

She denied that she gave statement before the IO as per Ex.P16.
28.

PW12 - Smt. Swetha, a neighbor of the deceased and circumstantial witness to the incident completely turned Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 hostile to the prosecution case and did not made any allegations against he accused.
Although she admitted that the accused and deceased were residing near to her house, she could not depose anything in respect of the incident.

29. PW13 - Mr.R.Prakash, ACP, Sheshadripuram Sub-Division, deposed about the part of the investigation conducted by him and he deposed that on 21.03.2024 he received the case file and recorded the statement of the witnesses, collected the documents and collected the video recording of the deceased while giving statement along with Sec.65(B) certificate as per Ex.P28 and collected postmortem report, caste certificate, FSL report and after completion of investigation he submitted the charge sheet.
30. In the cross examination, the learned counsel for the accused denied the entire manner in which the investigation was conducted and suggested that a false case has been filed against the accused.

sentences.text: PW14 - Mr. Basappa G.Dange, Head Constable, deposed that on 18.03.2024 he video graphed the statement of the victim in his 10+R One Plus mobile phone and also snapped photographs.
He gave certificate U/sec.65(B) of Indian Evidence Act as per Ex.P28 and he identified the DVD as per Ex.P29.
Mr. Vijaykumar Biradar, PSI deposed that on 18.03.2024 at 5.20 pm he received Ex.P1 statement of the victim through PW1 and registered a crime case as per Ex.P30/FIR.
On 19.03.2024 he conducted mahazar in the place of occurrence, recovery of MO1 to 4 articles, snapped Ex.P8 and 9 photographs and sent the articles for FSL examination.
On the same day he caused arrest of the accused and remanded him to judicial custody.

He recorded the statement of the pancha witnesses,
collected the caste certificate and handed over the investigation to ACP.
In the cross-examination learned defense counsel denied about the victim giving statement before him.
This is all the evidence placed by the prosecution in support of its case.
In the instant case, the accused has been charged for abetting the deceased to commit suicide and subjecting her to mental and physical cruelty on the demand of money for drinking alcohol.
He also being charged U/sec.3(2)(v) of SC & ST Act for committing the offenses under IPC which is punishable for 10 years or more.

It is settled position of law that in order to sustain conviction U/sec.306 of IPC, the prosecution has to prove the ingredients of Sec.306 of IPC.
34.

In the case of Geo Varghese v. State of Rajasthan and Another, reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 873, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as below:
"What is required to constitute an alleged abetment of suicide under Section 306 IPC is there must be an allegation of either direct or indirect act of incitement to the commission of offence of suicide and mere allegations of harassment of the deceased by another person would not be sufficient in itself, unless, there are allegations of such actions on the part of the accused which compelled the commission of Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 suicide.

entities.text: Geo Varghese v. State of Rajasthan and Another, reported in 2021 SCC Online SC 873
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, if the person committing suicide is hypersensitive and the allegations attributed to the accused is otherwise not ordinarily expected to induce a similarly situated person to take the extreme step of committing suicide, it would be unsafe to hold the accused guilty of abetment of suicide.".

35. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of M.Mohan v. State of Tamilnadu reported in (2011)3 SCC 626 held the following;
"Before holding an accused guilty of an offence under Section 306 of IPC, the court must scrupulously examine the facts and circumstances of the case and also assesses the evidence adduced before it in order to find out whether the cruelty and harassment meted out to the victim had left the victim with no other alternative, but to commit suicide.

entities.text: M.Mohan v. State of Tamilnadu reported in (2011)3 SCC 626
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also to be borne in mind that in cases of alleged abetment of Vyalikaval Ps vs Paneer Selvam on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92500410/
8 suicide, there must be proof of direct or indirect acts of incitement to the commission of suicide.

Merely on the allegation of harassment without Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 there being any positive action proximate to the time of occurrence on the part of the accused which led or compelled the person to commit suicide, conviction in terms of Section 306 of IPC is not sustainable".
36.
Bearing the aforesaid principals in mind, the evidence laid by the prosecution witnesses has to be considered.

As per the prosecution case, the deceased committed suicide due to the harassment given by the accused on the demand of money for drinking alcohol and also for the reason that he used to abuse her by taking her caste name.
To establish these facts, the prosecution has examined the children of the deceased as PW.4 and 5.
children of the deceased are the best eyewitnesses to the incident, as the quarrels between husband and wife most of the times take place inside the house.

37. According to the version portrayed by the prosecution, the accused persistently harassed the deceased by not taking care of the family, utilizing all his earnings for Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 alcohol drinking and when he fall short of money, he used to harass the deceased to give money for drinking alcohol.
Further the accused also used to assault when she failed to give money to the accused.
Except these allegations, there are no other allegations of harassment in the entire charge sheet materials.
38. In order to establish these circumstances, the prosecution examined the children of the deceased as PW.4 and 5.
However, both PW.4 and 5 did not deposed anything against the accused regarding any harassment being made on the deceased.
They both turned hostile to the prosecution case.
One more circumstantial witness PW.9 - Palani, brother of the accused, also failed to depose any incriminating evidence against the accused.
Similarly, the mother and sister of the deceased though hearsay witnesses to the incident, have failed to make any allegations against the accused towards the charges leveled against him.
A neighbor of the deceased PW.12 - Swetha, also turned hostile to the prosecution case.
Except the official witnesses, none of the independent eye witnesses have supported the prosecution case.
However, the I.O. has recorded the statement of the deceased while she was alive and taking treatment in the Hospital in Burns Ward of Victoria Hospital.
The incident took place on 17.03.2024 around 7 p.m., inside the house and the statement of the deceased is recorded on 18.03.2024 at 17.20 hours by PW.1 - WPC - Smt.Sandhya T.N.

The evidence of PW.1 indicates that she recorded the statement of the victim when the PSI was asking questions to the victim, she wrote the statement of the victim in her own handwriting in the Hospital.
40.
However, in the cross-examination, PW.1 admitted that the Doctor certified the fitness of the victim in his Chambers as per Ex.D1.
It was suggested by the learned defence counsel that the victim was not in a position to give any statement before the police as she was fully burnt up to 90%.
But to contradict the said version, the I.O. has also video-graphed the process of recorded the statement with the help of the H.C. - PW.14 - Basappa G.Dange.

The said video file is down loaded into a CD Vyalikaval Ps vs Paneer Selvam on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92500410/
9 and it is produced and marked as Ex.P29 along with section 65B Certificate as per Ex.P31.

sentences.text: PW.14 - Basappa Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 G.Dange, deposed in his evidence that he recorded the statement of the victim in his 10+ R Oneplus mobile phone and later he copied the same into a DVD and gave it to the I.O. along with Ex.P28/section 65B certificate.
41. Surprisingly, none of the prosecution witnesses were shown with the video recording.
Except marking the DVD as per Ex.P29, none of the witnesses identified the deceased and deposed about the deceased giving statement.

Since Ex.P29/DVD being secondary evidence, it is produced along with Section 65B certificate as per Ex.P28 and it fulfills the mandatory requirements of the certification and hence the video clipping can be looked into.

42. Upon carefully going through the said video recording which is made available in Ex.P29/DVD,
it indicates that though the victim was fully burnt, yet she was conscious and capable enough to give her statement.
She understood the questions being asked by the PSI and she gave her reply.
Her statement reveals that she was being scolded by the accused Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 for not giving money and the accused used to quarrel for trivial reasons.
The deceased was not happy with the behavior of the accused and by getting frustrated, she decided to commit suicide.
Hence, she poured kerosene and set herself on fire.
43. Ex.P1/statement is not completely in consonance with the statement made by the deceased in the video file.
Only few words were spoken by the deceased in the Hospital before the PSI and all she deposed is that she was not happy with the behavior of the accused and hence, she committed suicide.

On going through the complete statement of the victim available in Ex.P29/DVD, it can be said that there was no compelling situation for the deceased to commit suicide and getting dejected in life, the deceased committed suicide.

Although she made few allegations against the accused for having abused her for not giving money, yet it does not constitute the ingredients of section 306 of IPC.
44.

Except the statement of the deceased at Ex.P29/DVD, there is no evidence available on record to draw Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 an inference of guilty against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 306 of IPC.
The prosecution has failed to prove all the ingredients of Section 306 IPC and consequently, failed to prove that the accused abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
The accused did not intentionally aide or instigated or abetted the deceased to commit suicide.

Hence,
the offence under Section 306 of IPC is not made out.
Accordingly, point no.2 is answered in the negative.
45. Coming to the offence under Section 498A of IPC, the prosecution has to prove that the accused being the husband of the deceased, subjected her to cruelty.

Explanation (a) of Section 498A of IPC defines the term cruelty as, any willful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health of the woman.
In the instant case, the deceased being unable to withstand the harassment of the accused, she committed suicide.
This conduct of the accused in demanding money for drinking alcohol, has driven the deceased to commit suicide.

Although, the victim has not eloborately Vyalikaval Ps vs Paneer Selvam on 29 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92500410/
10 Spl.C.C.No. 888/2024 spoken about the nature of cruelty and harassment meted out to her, yet her statement is sufficient to hold that the accused subjected the deceased to cruelty and thereby he committed an offence under Section 498A of IPC.
Hence, he is found guilty of the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
Accordingly, I answer point no. 1 in the affirmative.

46. In so far as the offence under Section 3 (2) (v) of SC ST Act is concerned, it can be said that when the charge under section 306 IPC is answered in the negative, automatically the charge under Section 3 (2) (v) of SC ST act do not survive for consideration.
Accordingly, I answer point No.3 in the negative.

47. Point No.4:- In view of my findings on point No.1 to 3 and the reasons discussed above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Acting under Section.235(1) of Cr.P.C., Accused is found guilty for the offense punishable U/sec.498A of IPC.
Spl .C.C.No. 888/2024 Acting under Section.235(1) of Cr.P.C., Accused is acquitted for the offences punishable under Section 306 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of SC and ST Act.

30.09.2025 ORDER ON SENTENCE Judgment pronounced convicting the accused for the offence punishable under S.498A of I.P.C. Heard the convict Paneer Selvam,
who is now aged 42 years on the point of sentence.
The convict is having a family comprising of three children and presently they are under the care and custody of their grand parents, who has no means to look after them.
He submitted that his children are struggling to get one time meal a day due to poverty.
